title: Filtered cohomology colimits on a site with finite cofinal coverings
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site and $\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ its category of abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $\mathcal B\subseteq\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C)$ and let $\mathrm{Cov}_0$ be a set of covering families. Assume that every family $\{U_a\to U\}_{a\in A}$ in $\mathrm{Cov}_0$ has finite index set $A$, has $U,U_a\in\mathcal B$, and has every nonempty iterated fibre product $U_{a_0}\times_U\cdots\times_U U_{a_r}$, for $r\geq0$, in $\mathcal B$. Assume also that every covering of every $U\in\mathcal B$ is refined by a family in $\mathrm{Cov}_0$ with target $U$: each arrow of the refining family factors through some arrow of the original covering. Let $D$ be a small filtered category, meaning nonempty with a cocone on every finite diagram, and let $F:D\to\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ be a diagram. Write $\varinjlim_DF$ for its colimit in abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] and $H^q(U,-)=R^q\Gamma(U,-)$ for right-derived evaluation [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. For every $U\in\mathcal B$ and $q\geq0$, the map induced by the colimit coprojections is an isomorphism $$\varinjlim_{d\in D}H^q(U,F_d)\longrightarrow H^q(U,\varinjlim_DF).$$ Here a nonempty iterated fibre product means a product of one or more factors, with repetitions permitted, not a requirement that its underlying space be nonempty.

proof.text: For each $V\in\mathcal B$, refine an arbitrary covering by a family in $\mathrm{Cov}_0$. Its finite index set supplies a refinement with finite image in the original index set, so $V$ is quasi-compact in the explicit sense of [lem-sfb-site-quasi-compact-section-colimit]. For a family in $\mathrm{Cov}_0$ every pairwise overlap belongs to $\mathcal B$ and hence is quasi-compact by the same argument. The isomorphism clause of that lemma therefore gives $\varinjlim_d G_d(V)\cong(\varinjlim_dG_d)(V)$ for every diagram $G$ and every $V\in\mathcal B$. Since $H^0(V,G)=G(V)$ by [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], these are exactly the required canonical comparisons in degree zero.

source.place: Tag 0739, lemma-colim-works-over-collection, first proof paragraph; Sites Tag 0738(4).

proof.text: Let $I:D\to\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ be any diagram of injective sheaves and put $J=\varinjlim_dI_d$. Fix $\mathcal U=\{V_a\to V\}_{a\in A}\in\mathrm{Cov}_0$. In degree $r\ge0$ its Cech complex [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex] is the product over the finite set $A^{r+1}$ of sections on the iterated overlaps. Step 1 applies to each overlap. Combining those canonical section comparisons with [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimits-commute-finite-limits] gives the canonical isomorphism $\varinjlim_d\check{\mathcal C}^r(\mathcal U,I_d)\cong\check{\mathcal C}^r(\mathcal U,J)$. These maps commute with the differentials: on a component indexed by $(a_0,\ldots,a_{r+1})$, both composites are the sum over $j$ of $(-1)^j$ times restriction along the projection omitting $a_j$, followed by the sheaf colimit coprojection. This equality is naturality of each coprojection, term by term. Each stage complex is exact in positive degrees by [lem-weil-pbc-site-injective-cech-acyclic]. For each $r>0$ apply [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-abelian-groups-exact] to the exact triple of stage groups in degrees $r-1,r,r+1$. The colimit triple is exact at its middle group, hence the displayed degreewise comparisons give $\check H^r(\mathcal U,J)=0$. If $A$ is empty all these terms are zero, so the same conclusion holds.

source.place: Tag 0739, final proof paragraph: finite Cech complexes, Tag 03AW and exact filtered colimits.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-cech-vanishing-criterion] to $J$, $\mathcal B$ and $\mathrm{Cov}_0$. Its first hypothesis is precisely the assumed membership of all positive-length iterated overlaps in $\mathcal B$; its second is the given cofinality; its third was proved in step 2 for every selected covering and every positive degree. Consequently $H^r(V,J)=0$ for every $V\in\mathcal B$ and $r>0$, for every filtered diagram $I$ of injectives. No assertion that the colimit sheaf itself is injective is needed.

source.place: Tag 0739, final paragraph, application of Tag 03F9, lemma-cech-vanish-collection.

proof.text: Fix $U\in\mathcal B$. The category of abelian sheaves is Grothendieck abelian by [lem-cbc-sieve-module-sheaves-grothendieck] at $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$: abelian groups are $\mathbf Z$-modules with the unique action and additive maps are linear, so abelian and $\mathbf Z$-module presheaves agree; both sheaf conditions concern underlying presheaves of sets. Let $T$ be the Grothendieck topology generated by $\operatorname{Cov}(\mathcal C)$. By [lem-trf-generated-precoverage-sheaf-criterion], a presheaf of sets $P$ is a $T$-sheaf iff it has unique amalgamations on every sieve $f^*\langle R\rangle$ with $R=\{U_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ a covering and $f:Y\to X$. Since fibre products exist, $f^*\langle R\rangle=\langle f^*R\rangle$ for the covering $f^*R=\{U_i\times_XY\to Y\}$: an arrow $g$ lies in either sieve iff $fg$ factors through some $U_i$. A matching family on the generated sieve of a family is the same as a family of sections on its members agreeing on pairwise fibre products, so unique amalgamation there is the equalizer condition for $f^*R$. Hence $T$-sheaves are exactly the abelian sheaves of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], with the same morphisms. Evaluation $v=\Gamma(U,-)$ is additive and left exact by [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Small filtered colimits exist and are exact in the source by [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaves-filtered-colimits-exact], and are exact in abelian groups by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-abelian-groups-exact]. Induct on $q$, with the degree-zero case supplied by step 1. In the successor step apply [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-filtered-colimit-successor] to $v$, $D$ and $n=q$: the inductive assumption is preservation for every $D$-diagram, and step 3 supplies $R^{q+1}v(\varinjlim I)=0$ for every injective-valued diagram. Its conclusion is preservation in degree $q+1$. Its comparison is the map induced by the colimit coprojections, as asserted.

source.place: Tag 0739, induction and natural comparison ladder; functorial injective embeddings are included in the cited successor lemma.
